performers: San Francisco Symphony Orchestra, Pierre Monteux; Naoum Blinder, violin
question: How can one musical idea change its apparent character?
intro: Forceful low-register orchestral music and a violin-and-harp reply establish the storyteller’s frame. The flowing Allegro transforms earlier material through changing accompaniment, key and orchestral weight.

cues.title: Two kinds of introduction
cues.text: The opening opposes a forceful orchestral phrase to the solo violin’s more flexible line. Their contrasting registers and articulation establish the frame before the flowing main movement.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Violin beside harp
cues.text: The solo violin’s decorated line is supported by harp chords. The combination leaves much of the orchestral register empty, making a single player audible without a concerto-sized accompaniment.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Motion beneath the melody
cues.text: The main Allegro uses moving string figures beneath longer melodic values. Hear the accompaniment’s repeated rise and fall separately from the broader line above it.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A composer who went to sea
cues.text: Rimsky-Korsakov entered naval college in 1856 and served aboard the Almaz on a voyage from 1862 to 1865. The sea was part of his experience, but the score is not a documentary account of that voyage.
cues.evidence: Historical note, not a timed musical event. Rimsky-Korsakov, My Musical Life, translated by Judah A. Joffe, second edition: chapter I (July 1856 departure for the Marine Corps); chapters III–V (Almaz assignment, October 1862 departure and the 1862–65 cruise); chapter VI (September 1865 transfer ashore to Saint Petersburg). https://s9.imslp.org/files/imglnks/usimg/7/72/IMSLP721391-PMLP52433-My_Musical_Life_eng_edt.pdf

cues.title: A motif changes its role
cues.text: The forceful opening idea is transformed within the flowing music. A theme can remain recognisable through its intervals while a new rhythm and accompaniment change its apparent character.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: Winds continue the phrase
cues.text: The score passes melodic material through woodwind colours as well as strings. Compare the sustained line with its new articulation rather than assuming that every change of instrument introduces a new theme.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A frame for many tales
cues.text: The suite takes its title from the storyteller in The Thousand and One Nights. Rimsky-Korsakov later described the movement headings as hints for the listener, not instructions to identify an event at every bar.
cues.evidence: Historical or source-context note; no timed musical event is asserted. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade

cues.title: Repetition changes the harmony
cues.text: Repeated figures can carry the music through different harmonic settings. Listen for the same contour returning at a new pitch level while the accompaniment preserves the sense of motion.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A quieter scale of sound
cues.text: A reduced instrumental combination can make a familiar idea seem more intimate without changing its identity. Follow the relation between a single melodic line and its supporting figures.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The recording’s named players
cues.text: The source credits the San Francisco Symphony Orchestra under Pierre Monteux, with Naoum Blinder as solo violinist. The sessions took place on 3–4 March 1942; the documentation does not assign this movement to one day separately.
cues.evidence: The Commons description and upstream transfer record name the orchestra, conductor and violinist, and give 3–4 March 1942 for the complete suite: https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=628862047 ; https://archive.org/metadata/Sheherazade/metadata . No day is assigned to this movement separately.

cues.title: The sea theme returns
cues.text: The later return restores the flowing main material after its intervening transformations. Compare the orchestral weight of the return with the first Allegro statement.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The composer conducted the premiere
cues.text: Rimsky-Korsakov wrote Scheherazade in 1888 and conducted its first performance in Saint Petersburg that November. The work’s four connected movements were conceived for the concert orchestra, not for a staged adaptation of the tales.
cues.evidence: Historical or source-context note; no timed musical event is asserted. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade

cues.title: An orchestral close in E
cues.text: The movement’s ending settles in E major after the earlier changes of key and texture. Listen through the last sustained sound without treating its decay as the beginning of the next movement.
cues.evidence: General listening point about the written movement, not an instrument entrance or bar-aligned claim at this timestamp. https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

transitions.title: A single line answers the orchestra
transitions.how: After the forceful opening and intervening wind chords, the texture contracts to solo violin with harp support. The change of register and freedom of articulation establishes the contrasting narrative frame.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: The 0:16 reduction is followed by a strong boundary at 0:30; brighter, more articulated sound at 0:35–0:45 corroborates the score’s exposed violin region. Written design: https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf

transitions.title: The frame releases flowing motion
transitions.how: The violin’s freer introductory line leads into the Allegro’s regular accompanying figures. Moving strings establish the sea-like surface while longer melodic values transform material heard in the introduction.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: The report’s strongest boundary is 1:08; brightness drops while recorded level rises across 1:05–1:15. Written design: https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf

transitions.title: Full scoring gives way
transitions.how: The first large rise subsides into a lighter contrasting region. Reduced orchestral weight makes a more articulated accompaniment and changing wind colour audible without abandoning the movement’s thematic connections.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: The 2:42 boundary precedes a drop from roughly −7 dB to −25 dB at 2:45 and a strong reduction in brightness. Written design: https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf

transitions.title: The texture gathers force again
transitions.how: The lighter episode is drawn back into larger-scale transformation of the movement’s figures. Repeated patterns and accumulating orchestral weight make the transition continuous even while the harmonic setting changes.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: Several boundaries at 3:10–3:40 lead to high levels at 3:50–4:10; 3:40 is a broad entry into the renewed larger texture. Written design: https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf

transitions.title: The flowing material returns broadly
transitions.how: After the quieter central passage, the sea material regains orchestral breadth. The return connects the movement to its earlier Allegro but changes the weight and harmonic course of the familiar figures.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: The strong 6:10 boundary precedes a rapid rise at 6:15–6:20 and sustained stronger levels through 6:55. Written design: https://www.laphil.com/works/scheherazade Score: https://archive.org/download/Cantorion_sheet_music_collection_5/a2f9ec91cec0e2d1d7dd842aa83ea8fb.pdf

transitions.title: The sea motion settles
transitions.how: The returning orchestral force gives way to a quieter closing span. Moving strings and sustained wind harmony continue the E-directed close at a smaller scale rather than reopening the central argument.
transitions.evidence: Approximate passage boundary, not a bar alignment. cache/analysis/rimsky-korsakov-scheherazade-sea.txt: Level drops markedly at 7:00 and remains lower through the final E-major-compatible passage; the score, not the chroma estimate alone, establishes the ending key. timeline.note: Opening phrase: low winds, brass and strings state the forceful unison idea (PDF p. 1).
Intervening wind-chord region after the opening attack; the report’s 0:16 change marks the broad reduction.
Violin-and-harp introductory frame, approximately anchored at the report’s 0:30 boundary.
Flowing Allegro: moving strings support the broad melodic line; the 1:08 boundary marks the changed texture.
First fuller sea passage: piccolo, brass and timpani reinforce winds and strings across the 1:50–2:40 high-level span.
Reduced contrasting region: wind and string dialogue after the strong 2:42 drop; not a claim that all listed instruments sustain every bar.
Central larger scoring: high winds, brass and timpani reinforce the string motion across the rise after 3:40 (including PDF p. 10).
Quieter central span: the 5:10 boundary reduces the larger scoring to more exposed wind and string roles.
Later sea-material expansion: broad fuller scoring returns after the 6:10 boundary (including PDF p. 18).
Closing reduction after 7:00: sustained winds and moving strings settle the preceding larger argument.
Final cadence region: divided cello writing yields to plucked string chords beneath held wind and horn harmony (PDF p. 23); broad anchor at 7:54.

composer.epithet: A naval officer turned teacher who made orchestral register and symmetrical scales the machinery of Russian fairy-tale opera.
facts: Naval College in Saint Petersburg; composition with Mily Balakirev, followed by intensive private study
Saint Petersburg Conservatory from 1871; inspector of naval bands, 1873–84
Married the pianist and composer Nadezhda Purgold in 1872; she assisted with arrangements and editorial work
Fifteen operas, three symphonies, orchestral suites and overtures, songs and teaching books
composer.background:
Rimsky-Korsakov was born in Tikhvin into a family with a tradition of naval service. He entered the Naval College in Saint Petersburg in 1856, while continuing piano lessons and attending opera. His teacher Fyodor Kanille introduced him to Balakirev in 1861. The young officer began a symphony before he had the theoretical equipment expected of a conservatory composition student. A naval voyage on the clipper Almaz took him abroad in 1862–65, interrupting regular contact with the circle while work on the symphony continued. Balakirev conducted the First Symphony in Saint Petersburg in 1865.

His early colleagues included Mussorgsky, Borodin and Cui. With Balakirev they became the group known as the Five, united by friendship and cultural argument despite their differing methods. Rimsky-Korsakov’s orchestral picture Sadko, first written in 1867, already connects a supernatural subject with an unusual pitch organisation. The sea musician’s underwater world encouraged scales and chord relationships outside ordinary major and minor. His experience of ships and oceans gave the subject a biographical setting.
